$$ \left\{\left(n\cdot A_{r}\cdot\alpha^{(r)}(i,j,k),i,j,k,\beta_{\textit{X},i,j,k}^{(r)},\beta^{(r)}_{\textit{Y},i,j,k},\beta^{(r)}_{\textit{Z},i,j,k}\right)\right\}_{r\in[6],i+j+k=2^{\ell}} $$

where the constraints are the same as those in Proposition 5.1.88 8 $o_{1/\varepsilon}(1)$ denotes a function $f(\varepsilon)$ where $f(\varepsilon)\to 0$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ . We also use $o_{1/\varepsilon}(n)$ to denote $o_{1/\varepsilon}(1)\cdot n$ .

In the remainder of this section, we prove Proposition 5.1.

### 5.1 Dividing into Regions

As in previous works [DWZ23, VXXZ24], we partition the $n$ -th tensor power of $\mathrm{CW}_{q}^{\otimes 2^{\ell-1}}$ into several “regions”. For each different region, we use a different permutation for the roles of the $X$ , $Y$ , $Z$ -dimensions. In [DWZ23, VXXZ24], they partition $(\mathrm{CW}_{q}^{\otimes 2^{\ell-1}})^{\otimes n}$ into three regions due to the fact that two out of the three dimensions are treated symmetrically in their algorithms. Since our method is more asymmetric, we need to partition $(\mathrm{CW}_{q}^{\otimes 2^{\ell-1}})^{\otimes n}$ into six regions instead. More specifically, we consider

$$ \bigl(\mathrm{CW}_{q}^{\otimes 2^{\ell-1}}\bigr)^{\otimes n}\equiv\bigotimes_{r=1}^{6}\bigl(\mathrm{CW}_{q}^{\otimes 2^{\ell-1}}\bigr)^{\otimes A_{r}\cdot n} $$

for $A_{1},\ldots,A_{6}\geq 0$ and $A_{1}+\cdots+A_{6}=1$ , and we denote the $r$ -th region by $\mathcal{T}^{(r)}$ .

In the following, we will focus on the analysis for $\mathcal{T}^{(1)}$ . The analysis for other regions is similar, but we permute the roles of the $X$ , $Y$ , $Z$ -dimensions in different regions. For simplicity, we will drop the superscript $(1)$ .

### 5.2 More Asymmetric Hashing

This hashing step is standard in all previous literature on applications of the laser method, and we only deviate from previous works at the end of this step. Nevertheless, we repeat the description of the hashing procedure for completeness.

Let $\alpha$ be a distribution on $\{(i,j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{3}\mid i+j+k=2^{\ell}\}$ , and let ${\alpha}_{\textit{X}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Y}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Z}}$ be the marginal distributions of $\alpha$ on the three dimensions respectively.

First, in $\mathcal{T}$ , we zero out the level- $\ell$ $X$ -blocks that are not consistent with ${\alpha}_{\textit{X}}$ , the level- $\ell$ $Y$ -blocks that are not consistent with ${\alpha}_{\textit{Y}}$ , and the level- $\ell$ $Z$ -block that are not consistent with ${\alpha}_{\textit{Z}}$ . Let $N_{\textup{BX}},N_{\textup{BY}},N_{\textup{BZ}}$ be the number of remaining $X$ , $Y$ , $Z$ -blocks respectively, $N_{{\alpha}_{\textit{X}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Y}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Z}}}$ be the number of remaining block triples, and $N_{\alpha}$ be the number of remaining block triples consistent with $\alpha$ . These values can be approximated in the standard way:

#### Claim 5.4.

$\displaystyle N_{\textup{BX}}=2^{H({\alpha}_{\textit{X}})\cdot A_{1}n\pm o(n)},\quad N_{\textup{BY}}=2^{H({\alpha}_{\textit{Y}})\cdot A_{1}n\pm o(n)},\quad N_{\textup{BZ}}=2^{H({\alpha}_{\textit{Z}})\cdot A_{1}n\pm o(n)},\phantom{\textbf{Claim X.X.}}$

$$ N_{\alpha}=2^{H(\alpha)\cdot A_{1}n\pm o(n)},\quad N_{{\alpha}_{\textit{X}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Y}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Z}}}=2^{(H(\alpha)+P_{\alpha})\cdot A_{1}n\pm o(n)}. $$

Let

$$ M_{0}\geq 8\cdot\frac{N_{{\alpha}_{\textit{X}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Y}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Z}}}}{N_{\textup{BX}}} $$

be an integer yet to be fixed, and let $M\in[M_{0},2M_{0}]$ be a prime number (its existence is guaranteed by Bertrand’s postulate). For random $b_{0},\{w_{t}\}_{t=0}^{n}\in\mathbb{Z}_{M}$ , we define three hash functions $h_{\textit{X}},h_{\textit{Y}},h_{\textit{Z}}:\{0,\ldots,2^{\ell}\}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{M}$ as:

$$ \displaystyle h_{\textit{X}}(I) \displaystyle=b_{0}+\left(\sum_{t=1}^{n}w_{t}\cdot I_{t}\right)\bmod M, \displaystyle h_{\textit{Y}}(J) \displaystyle=b_{0}+\left(w_{0}+\sum_{t=1}^{n}w_{t}\cdot J_{t}\right)\bmod M, \displaystyle h_{\textit{Z}}(K) \displaystyle=b_{0}+\frac{1}{2}\left(w_{0}+\sum_{t=1}^{n}w_{t}\cdot(2^{\ell}-K_{t})\right)\bmod M. $$

Let $B$ be the Salem-Spencer subset of $\mathbb{Z}_{M}$ of size $M^{1-o(1)}$ from Theorem 3.7 that contains no three-term arithmetic progressions. Then we zero out all the level- $\ell$ $X$ -blocks $X_{I}$ where $h_{\textit{X}}(I)\not\in B$ , all the level- $\ell$ $Y$ -blocks $Y_{I}$ where $h_{\textit{Y}}(J)\not\in B$ , and all the level- $\ell$ $Z$ -blocks $X_{K}$ where $h_{\textit{Z}}(K)\not\in B$ .

Note that by definition of the hash functions, we have $h_{\textit{X}}(I)+h_{\textit{Y}}(J)=2h_{\textit{Z}}(K)$ for any block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ (as $h_{\textit{X}}(I),h_{\textit{Y}}(J),h_{\textit{Z}}(K)\in Z_{M}$ , this equation holds modulo $M$ if we view them as integers in $\mathbb{Z}$ ). Therefore, since we only keep blocks whose hash values belong to the Salem-Spencer set $B$ , all remaining block triples $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ must have $h_{\textit{X}}(I)=h_{\textit{Y}}(J)=h_{\textit{Z}}(K)=b$ for some $b\in B$ . Now for every $b\in B$ , if there are two block triples $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ and $X_{I}Y_{J^{\prime}}Z_{K^{\prime}}$ that are both hashed to $b$ and share the same $X$ -block $X_{I}$ , we zero out $X_{I}$ .

We call the tensor after this zeroing out $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{hash}}$ and note that every level- $\ell$ $X$ -block is in a unique level- $\ell$ block triple in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{hash}}$ . We highlight that this is the start of the main deviation from previous works. In previous works [DWZ23, VXXZ24], after this step all level- $\ell$ $X$ -blocks and $Y$ -blocks are in unique block triples; in earlier works [Str86, Vas12, DS13, LG14, AV21], all level- $\ell$ blocks are in unique block triples.

We summarize the properties of this hashing procedure and $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{hash}}$ in the following lemma.

#### Lemma 5.5 (Properties of more asymmetric hashing).

The above described procedure and its output $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{hash}}$ satisfy the following:

- 1. (Implicit in [CW90], see also [DWZ23]) For any level- $\ell$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}\in\mathcal{T}$ and every bucket $b\in\mathbb{Z}_{M}$ , we have

$$ \myPr\left[\vphantom{\sum}h_{\textit{X}}(I)=h_{\textit{Y}}(J)=h_{\textit{Z}}(K)=b\right]=\frac{1}{M^{2}}. $$

Furthermore, for any $b\in\mathbb{Z}_{M}$ we have that any two different block triples $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K},X_{I}Y_{J^{\prime}}Z_{K^{\prime}}\in\mathcal{T}$ that share the same $X$ -block satisfy

$$ \myPr\left[\vphantom{\sum}h_{\textit{X}}(I)=h_{\textit{Y}}(J^{\prime})=h_{\textit{Z}}(K^{\prime})=b\;\middle|\;h_{\textit{X}}(I)=h_{\textit{Y}}(J)=h_{\textit{Z}}(K)=b\right]=\frac{1}{M}. $$

The same holds for different blocks that share the same $Y$ -block or $Z$ -block.

- 2. (Similar to [VXXZ24, Claim 5.6]) For every $b\in B$ and every level- $\ell$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}\in\mathcal{T}$ consistent with $\alpha$ , we have

$$ \myPr\left[X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}\in\mathcal{T}_{\textup{hash}}\;\middle|\;h_{\textit{X}}(I)=h_{\textit{Y}}(J)=h_{\textit{Z}}(K)=b\right]\geq\frac{3}{4}. $$

- 3. ([VXXZ24, Claim 5.7])

$$ \E[\textup{number of level-$\ell$ triples in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{hash}}$}]\geq N_{\alpha}\cdot M_{0}^{-1-o(1)}. $$

### 5.3 $Y$ -Compatibility Zero-Out

Let

$$ S^{(I,J,K)}_{i,j,k}\coloneqq\{t\in[n]\mid I_{t}=i,J_{t}=j,K_{t}=k\} $$

and

$$ S^{(J)}_{*,j,*}\coloneqq\{t\in[n]\mid J_{t}=j\},\quad S^{(K)}_{*,*,k}\coloneqq\{t\in[n]\mid K_{t}=k\}. $$

We will drop the superscripts if the context is clear.99 9 If we follow our general rules for notations described at the beginning of Section 5 strictly, $S_{*,j,*}^{(J)}$ and $S_{*,*,k}^{(K)}$ would be denoted as $S_{*,j,*}^{(I,J,K)}$ and $S_{*,*,k}^{(I,J,K)}$ , but notice that the extra superscripts can be dropped as they do not affect the values of $S_{*,j,*}^{(I,J,K)}$ and $S_{*,*,k}^{(I,J,K)}$ .

Recall that in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{hash}}$ , every level- $\ell$ $X$ -block is in a unique block triple, so given a level- $\ell$ block $X_{I}$ , we can uniquely determine the level- $\ell$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ containing it. For any $i,j,k$ , and any level-1 block $X_{\hat{I}}\in X_{I}$ , if $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{I},S_{i,j,k})\neq\beta_{\textit{X},i,j,k}$ , we zero out $X_{\hat{I}}$ .

The overall goal of this step is to zero out some level-1 $Y$ -blocks, so that each remaining level-1 $Y$ -block belongs to a unique level- $\ell$ block triple as well.

#### 5.3.1 $Y$ -Compatibility Zero-Out I

Given any level-1 $Y$ -block $Y_{\hat{J}}$ , if there exists a $j$ such that $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{*,j,*})\neq\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Y},*,j,*}$ , then we zero out $Y_{\hat{J}}$ . Eventually, the goal is to obtain independent copies of the interface tensor with complete split distributions $\left\{\beta_{\textit{X},i,j,k},\beta_{\textit{Y},i,j,k},\beta_{\textit{Z},i,j,k}\right\}_{i+j+k=2^{\ell}}$ . For any $Y_{\hat{J}}\in Y_{J}$ , if $Y_{\hat{J}}$ belongs to such an interface tensor, then we must have $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{*,j,*})=\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Y},*,j,*}$ for every $j$ . This is because if there exist $X_{\hat{I}}\in X_{I}$ and $Z_{\hat{K}}\in Z_{K}$ such that $X_{\hat{I}}Y_{\hat{J}}Z_{\hat{K}}\in X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ , where $X_{\hat{I}}Y_{\hat{J}}Z_{\hat{K}}$ is consistent with the complete split distributions and $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ is consistent with $\alpha$ , then one can verify that $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{*,j,*})=\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Y},*,j,*}$ for every $j$ regardless of what $X_{\hat{I}}$ and $Z_{\hat{K}}$ are. So it does not hurt to zero out these $Y_{\hat{J}}$ blocks. We call the tensor obtained after this zero-out $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{comp}}^{Y}$ .

Next, we define the notion of compatibility for level-1 $Y$ -blocks, which is similar to the definition of compatibility in [VXXZ24].

#### Definition 5.6 ( $Y$ -Compatibility).

Given a level- $\ell$ triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ and a level- $1$ $Y$ -block $Y_{\hat{J}}\in Y_{J}$ , we say that $Y_{\hat{J}}$ is compatible with $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ if the following hold:

- 1. For every $(i,j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{3}$ with $i+j+k=2^{\ell}$ and $k=0$ , $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{i,j,k})=\beta_{\textit{Y},i,j,k}$ .

- 2. For every index $j\in\{0,1,\ldots,2^{\ell}\}$ , $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{*,j,*})=\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Y},*,j,*}$ .

#### Claim 5.7.

In $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{comp}}^{Y}$ , for every level-1 block triple $X_{\hat{I}}Y_{\hat{J}}Z_{\hat{K}}$ and the level- $\ell$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ that contains it, $Y_{\hat{J}}$ is compatible with $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ .

#### Proof.

It is easy to see that Item 2 is satisfied by our procedure since we will zero out all the level-1 $Y_{\hat{J}}$ block if there exists $j\in\{0,\ldots,2^{\ell}\}$ such that $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{*,j,*})\neq\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Y},*,j,*}$ . So it suffices to show Item 1.

Note that all the remaining level-1 $X$ -blocks $X_{\hat{I}}$ satisfy $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{I},S_{i,j,k})=\beta_{\textit{X},i,j,k}$ for all $(i,j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{3}$ with $i+j+k=2^{\ell}$ due to the first zero-out in Section 5.3 on level- $1$ $X$ -blocks. Now consider $(i,j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{3}$ with $k=0$ and $i+j+k=2^{\ell}$ . In a remaining level- $1$ triple $X_{\hat{I}}Y_{\hat{J}}Z_{\hat{K}}$ , we must have $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{I},S_{i,j,k})=\beta_{\textit{X},i,j,k}$ . Then since $k=0$ , we have $K_{t}=0$ for all $t\in S_{i,j,k}$ , i.e., $(\hat{K}_{(t-1)\cdot 2^{\ell-1}+1},\hat{K}_{(t-1)\cdot 2^{\ell-1}+2},\dots,\hat{K}_{t\cdot 2^{\ell-1}})=\vec{0}$ . Since we have for each $\hat{t}\in\{(t\!-\!1)\cdot 2^{\ell-1}\!+\!1,\,\dots\,,\,t\cdot 2^{\ell-1}\}$ , $\hat{I}_{\hat{t}}+\hat{J}_{\hat{t}}+\hat{K}_{\hat{t}}=2$ , we have for all $t\in S_{i,j,k}$ ,

$$ \left(\hat{J}_{(t-1)\cdot 2^{\ell-1}+1},\hat{J}_{(t-1)\cdot 2^{\ell-1}+2},\dots,\hat{J}_{t\cdot 2^{\ell-1}}\right)=\vec{2}-\left(\hat{I}_{(t-1)\cdot 2^{\ell-1}+1},\hat{I}_{(t-1)\cdot 2^{\ell-1}+2},\dots,\hat{I}_{t\cdot 2^{\ell-1}}\right). $$

So for every length- $2^{\ell-1}$ tuple $L\in\{0,1,2\}^{2^{\ell-1}}$ , we must have

$$ \textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{i,j,k})(L)=\textsf{{split}}(\hat{I},S_{i,j,k})(\vec{2}-L)=\beta_{\textit{X},i,j,k}(\vec{2}-L). $$

By Remark 5.2, we have that $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{i,j,k})(L)=\beta_{\textit{X},i,j,k}(\vec{2}-L)=\beta_{\textit{Y},i,j,k}(L)$ as desired. ∎

#### 5.3.2 $Y$ -Compatibility Zero-Out II: Unique Triple

After the previous step, it is guaranteed that every remaining level-1 $Y$ -block $Y_{\hat{J}}$ is compatible with all the level- $\ell$ block triples containing it by Claim 5.7. In order to ensure that each remaining $Y_{\hat{J}}$ belongs to a unique triple after further zero-outs, it suffices to guarantee that $Y_{\hat{J}}$ belongs to a unique triple that it is compatible with. Therefore, given any $Y_{\hat{J}}$ that is compatible with more than one triple, we zero it out.

After this step, each remaining $Y_{\hat{J}}$ belongs to a unique triple, and additionally $Y_{\hat{J}}$ is compatible with this triple.

#### 5.3.3 $Y$ -Usefulness Zero-Out

At this point, each remaining level-1 block $Y_{\hat{J}}$ belongs to a unique triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ . So now we can check whether $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{i,j,k})=\beta_{\textit{Y},i,j,k}$ for all $i,j,k$ , and zero out $Y_{\hat{J}}$ if there exists some $i,j,k$ such that the equality does not hold.

For convenience, we define the following notion of usefulness.

#### Definition 5.8 ( $Y$ -Usefulness).

Given a level- $\ell$ triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ and a level-1 block $Y_{\hat{J}}\in Y_{J}$ , we say $Y_{\hat{J}}$ is useful for $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ if $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{i,j,k})=\beta_{\textit{Y},i,j,k}$ for every $i,j,k$ .

Using the above definition, this step is equivalent to zeroing out every level-1 block $Y_{\hat{J}}$ that is not useful for the unique triple containing it. We call the remaining tensor after this step $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Y}$ .

### 5.4 $Z$ -Compatibility Zero-Out

After $Y$ -compatibility zero-outs, every level- $1$ $Y$ -block $Y_{\hat{J}}\in Y_{J}$ must be in a unique level- $\ell$ triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ and the same holds for every level- $1$ $X$ -block $X_{\hat{I}}$ as well. The goal of this step is to zero out some level- $1$ $Z$ -blocks $Z_{\hat{K}}$ so that every level- $1$ $Z$ -block is also in a unique level- $\ell$ triple. We note that this step is similar to the compatibility zero-out and usefulness zero-out steps in [VXXZ24] and Definitions 5.9 and 5.11 are identical to the definition of compatibility and usefulness respectively in [VXXZ24].

#### 5.4.1 $Z$ -Compatibility Zero-Out I

Given any level-1 block $Z_{\hat{K}}\in Z_{K}$ , we zero out $Z_{\hat{K}}$ if there exists a $k$ such that $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{K},S_{*,*,k})\neq\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Z},*,*,k}$ . We call the obtained tensor $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{comp}}^{Z}$ .

Next, we are ready to define compatibility for level- $1$ $Z_{\hat{K}}$ blocks.

#### Definition 5.9 ( $Z$ -Compatibility).

Given a level- $\ell$ triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ and a level- $1$ $Z$ -block $Z_{\hat{K}}\in Z_{K}$ , we say that $Z_{\hat{K}}$ is compatible with $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ if the following hold:

- 1. For every $(i,j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{3}$ with $i+j+k=2^{\ell}$ , $i=0$ or $j=0$ , there is $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{K},S_{i,j,k})=\beta_{\textit{Z},i,j,k}$ .

- 2. For every index $k\in\{0,1,\ldots,2^{\ell}\}$ , $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{K},S_{*,*,k})=\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Z},*,*,k}$ .

#### Claim 5.10 ([VXXZ24, Claim 5.9]).

In $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{comp}}^{Z}$ , for every level-1 block triple $X_{\hat{I}}Y_{\hat{J}}Z_{\hat{K}}$ and the level- $\ell$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ that contains it, $Z_{\hat{K}}$ is compatible with $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ .

#### 5.4.2 $Z$ -Compatibility Zero-Out II: Unique Triple

Now in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{comp}}^{Z}$ , every level- $1$ $Z$ -block $Z_{\hat{K}}$ is compatible with the level- $\ell$ triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ containing it, but there can be multiple level- $\ell$ triples containing the level- $1$ block $Z_{\hat{K}}$ . So in this step, we zero out $Z_{\hat{K}}$ if it is compatible with more than one level- $\ell$ triple. Then the remaining tensor satisfies the property that every level- $1$ $Z_{\hat{K}}$ is contained in a unique level- $\ell$ triple, and $Z_{\hat{K}}$ is compatible with that triple.

#### 5.4.3 $Z$ -Usefulness Zero-Out

For convenience, we also define the notion of usefulness for $Z$ -blocks.

#### Definition 5.11 ( $Z$ -Usefulness).

Given a level- $\ell$ triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ and a level-1 block $Z_{\hat{K}}\in Z_{K}$ , we say that $Z_{\hat{K}}$ is useful for $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ if $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{K},S_{i,j,k})=\beta_{\textit{Z},i,j,k}$ for every $i,j,k$ .

We zero out every level-1 block $Z_{\hat{K}}$ that is not useful for the unique triple containing it and call the remaining tensor $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Z}$ .

### 5.5 Fixing Holes

At this stage, the subtensor of the remaining tensor $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Z}$ over $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ is a subtensor of the following tensor

$$ \mathcal{T}^{*}=\bigotimes_{i+j+k=2^{\ell}}T_{i,j,k}^{\otimes A_{1}\cdot\alpha(i,j,k)\cdot n}[\beta_{\textit{X},i,j,k},\beta_{\textit{Y},i,j,k},\beta_{\textit{Z},i,j,k}], $$

i.e., it is the level- $\ell$ interface tensor with parameter list

$$ \left\{\left(A_{1}\cdot\alpha(i,j,k)\cdot n,i,j,k,\beta_{\textit{X},i,j,k},\beta_{\textit{Y},i,j,k},\beta_{\textit{Z},i,j,k}\right)\right\}_{i+j+k=2^{\ell}}. $$

More precisely:

#### Claim 5.12.

For any level- $\ell$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ contained in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{hash}}$ , the subtensor of $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Z}$ restricted to the level- $\ell$ blocks $X_{I},Y_{J},Z_{K}$ is a subtensor of $\mathcal{T}^{*}$ , where the missing variables in this subtensor are exactly those level-1 blocks $Y_{\hat{J}}$ that are compatible with multiple level- $\ell$ triples in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{comp}}^{Y}$ and level-1 blocks $Z_{\hat{K}}$ that are compatible with multiple level- $\ell$ triples in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{comp}}^{Z}$ .

#### Proof.

We first show that for any level- $\ell$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{hash}}$ , $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Z}|_{X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}}$ is a subtensor of $\mathcal{T}^{*}$ . Note that we already have

$$ \mathcal{T}_{\textup{hash}}\big|_{X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}}\equiv\bigotimes_{i+j+k=2^{\ell}}T_{i,j,k}^{\otimes A_{1}\cdot\alpha(i,j,k)\cdot n}, $$

so it suffices to show that all the level-1 triples $X_{\hat{I}}Y_{\hat{J}}Z_{\hat{K}}$ remaining in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Z}$ satisfy the following for all $i,j,k$ :

- 1. $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{I},S_{i,j,k})=\beta_{\textit{X},i,j,k}$ ,

- 2. $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{i,j,k})=\beta_{\textit{Y},i,j,k}$ ,

- 3. $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{K},S_{i,j,k})=\beta_{\textit{Z},i,j,k}$ .

Note that Item 1 is automatically satisfied due to the step in $Y$ -compatibility zero-out, since we have zeroed out any level-1 $X_{\hat{I}}\in X_{I}$ with $i,j,k$ such that $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{I},S_{i,j,k})\neq\beta_{\textit{X},i,j,k}$ . Item 2 is satisfied due to $Y$ -usefulness zero-out and Item 3 is satisfied due to $Z$ -usefulness zero-out. Thus, $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Z}|_{X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}}$ is a subtensor of $T^{*}$ .

Now we analyze what the missing $Y$ -variables are. Note that for level-1 $Y_{\hat{J}}$ blocks, we have enforced the following conditions:

- (1) In $Y$ -compatibility zero-out I, we enforce that $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{*,j,*})=\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Y},*,j,*}$ .

- (2) In $Y$ -compatibility zero-out II, we enforce that each $\hat{J}$ is compatible with a unique level- $\ell$ triple.

- (3) In $Y$ -usefulness zero-out, we enforce that $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{i,j,k})=\beta_{i,j,k}$ for every $i,j,k$ .

We claim that condition (3) is strictly stronger than condition (1), because by definition, (3) implies

$$ \displaystyle\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{*,j,*}) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{\sum_{i,k}\alpha(i,j,k)}\sum_{i+k=2^{\ell}-j}\alpha(i,j,k)\cdot\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{i,j,k}) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{\sum_{i,k}\alpha(i,j,k)}\sum_{i+k=2^{\ell}-j}\alpha(i,j,k)\cdot\beta_{\textit{Y},i,j,k} \displaystyle=\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Y},*,j,*}. $$

Also, enforcing condition (3) does not create missing $Y$ -variables, as it is enforcing the necessary complete split distribution condition in the definition of $\mathcal{T}^{*}$ . Thus, the missing variables are exactly due to enforcing condition (2), i.e., the level-1 $Y_{\hat{J}}$ blocks that are compatible with more than one level- $\ell$ triple. Similarly, the missing $Z$ variables are exactly those level-1 $Z_{\hat{K}}$ blocks that are compatible with more than one level- $\ell$ triple. ∎

Furthermore, observe that $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Z}|_{X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}}$ is level-1-independent for different block triples $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ : The $X$ -blocks are level- $\ell$ -independent after the zero-out in the asymmetric hashing step; for $Y$ and $Z$ -blocks, by Claims 5.7 and 5.10, each level-1 block is compatible with all the level- $\ell$ triples containing it, and we zeroed out all level-1 $Y$ and $Z$ -blocks that are compatible with multiple level- $\ell$ triples, so the remaining level-1 $Y$ and $Z$ -blocks belong to unique level- $\ell$ triples. As a result,

$$ \mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Z}\,=\bigoplus_{X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}\;\textup{remaining}}\mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Z}\big|_{X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}} $$

is a direct sum of broken copies of $\mathcal{T}^{*}$ .

To fix the holes, we need to first bound the fraction of holes in the broken copies of $\mathcal{T}^{*}$ contained in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Z}$ . Similar to the analysis in [VXXZ24], we introduce the notion of typicalness for level- $1$ $Y$ -blocks and $Z$ -blocks and define the values $p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}$ and $p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}$ respectively. ## 6 Constituent Stage

In the level- $\ell$ constituent stage, the algorithm takes as input a collection of level- $\ell$ $\varepsilon$ -interface tensors, and degenerates them into the tensor product between a matrix multiplication tensor (obtained from the parts of the interface tensor where $i_{t}=0$ , $j_{t}=0$ , or $k_{t}=0$ ) and a collection of independent copies of level- $(\ell-1)$ $\varepsilon^{\prime}$ -interface tensors for some $\varepsilon^{\prime}>0$ (obtained from the other parts).

More specifically, given an $\varepsilon$ -interface tensor with parameters

$$ \{(n_{t},i_{t},j_{t},k_{t},\beta_{\textit{X},t},\beta_{\textit{Y},t},\beta_{\textit{Z},t})\}_{t\in[s]}, $$

we use the notation $n:=\sum_{t}n_{t}$ and $N:=2^{\ell-1}\cdot n$ .

$$ \beta_{\textit{X},t}(L)=\beta_{\textit{Z},t}(\vec{2}-L). $$

The same holds between $\beta_{\textit{X},t}$ and $\beta_{\textit{Y},t}$ when $k_{t}=0$ , and between $\beta_{\textit{Y},t}$ and $\beta_{\textit{Z},t}$ when $i_{t}=0$ .

Eventually, we want to ensure that the subtensor of $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{useful}}^{Z}$ restricted to each level- $(\ell-1)$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ is isomorphic to

$$ \mathcal{T}^{*}=\bigotimes_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}\;\bigotimes_{i^{\prime}+j^{\prime}+k^{\prime}=2^{\ell-1}}T_{i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime}}^{\otimes A_{t,1}\cdot(\alpha_{t}(i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime})+\alpha_{t}(i_{t}-i^{\prime},j_{t}-j^{\prime},k_{t}-k^{\prime}))\cdot n_{t}}[\beta_{\textit{X},t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime}},\beta_{\textit{Y},t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime}},\beta_{\textit{Z},t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime}}]. $$

Similar to before, there are some holes caused by our degeneration process. The three types of holes are the following:

- • The input of the constituent stage does not include all level- $1$ blocks, as we enforce some $\varepsilon$ -approximate complete split distribution on the input. As analyzed in the previous work [VXXZ24], the fraction of this type of holes can be upper bounded by $1/n^{2}$ in all three dimensions. The high-level intuition is that, if we take a random level- $1$ block from $\mathcal{T}^{*}$ , it will likely be $\varepsilon$ -approximate consistent with the complete split distribution in the input. Thus, most level- $1$ blocks from $\mathcal{T}^{*}$ should appear in the input, which implies the fraction of this type of holes is small.

- • The holes on $Y$ -blocks caused by $Y$ -compatibility zero-outs. These holes were not considered before, so the main focus of the analysis will be this case.

- • The holes on $Z$ -blocks caused by $Z$ -compatibility zero-outs. The analysis of these holes is similar to the previous work [VXXZ24], so we will omit most proofs of this case in the following.

Next, we focus on holes on level-1 blocks caused by compatibility zero-outs. These are the fractions of (typical) $Y_{\hat{J}}$ and $Z_{\hat{K}}$ that are compatible with multiple level- $(\ell-1)$ triples. Similar to before, we define typicalness, $p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}$ , and $p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}$ .

#### Definition 6.14 ( $Y$ -Typicalness).

A level-1 $Y$ -block $Y_{\hat{J}}$ in some level- $(\ell-1)$ $Y$ -block $Y_{J}$ is typical if $\|\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{t,*,*,*})-\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Y},t,*,*,*}\|_{\infty}\leq\varepsilon$ for every $t\in[s^{\prime}]$ .

#### Definition 6.15 ( $Z$ -Typicalness).

A level-1 $Z$ -block $Z_{\hat{K}}$ in some level- $(\ell-1)$ $Z$ -block $Z_{K}$ is typical if $\|\textsf{{split}}(\hat{K},S_{t,*,*,*})-\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Z},t,*,*,*}\|_{\infty}\leq\varepsilon$ for every $t\in[s^{\prime}]$ .

#### Definition 6.16 ( $p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}$ ).

For fixed $Y_{\hat{J}}$ and $Y_{J}$ where $Y_{\hat{J}}\in Y_{J}$ and $\hat{J}$ has level- $\ell$ complete split distributions $\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}$ , we define $p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}^{*}(\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]})$ as the probability that a uniformly random level- $(\ell-1)$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ consistent with $\{\alpha_{t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}$ is compatible with $Y_{\hat{J}}$ . We further define

$$ p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}\,\coloneqq\max_{\begin{subarray}{c}\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}\,:\\
\left\lVert\xi_{\textit{Y},t}-\beta_{\textit{Y},t}\right\rVert_{\infty}\leq\varepsilon\;\forall t\end{subarray}}p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}^{*}(\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}). $$

#### Definition 6.17 ( $p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}$ ).

For fixed $Z_{\hat{K}}$ and $Z_{K}$ where $Z_{\hat{K}}\in Z_{K}$ and $\hat{K}$ has level- $\ell$ complete split distributions $\{\xi_{\textit{Z},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}$ , we define $p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}^{*}(\{\xi_{\textit{Z},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]})$ as the probability that a uniformly random level- $(\ell-1)$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ consistent with $\{\alpha_{t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}$ is compatible with $Z_{\hat{K}}$ . We further define

$$ p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}\,\coloneqq\max_{\begin{subarray}{c}\{\xi_{\textit{Z},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}\,:\\
\left\lVert\xi_{\textit{Z},t}-\beta_{\textit{Z},t}\right\rVert_{\infty}\leq\varepsilon\;\forall t\end{subarray}}p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}^{*}(\{\xi_{\textit{Z},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}). $$

Similar to before, $p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}^{*}(\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]})$ does not depend on the choice of $Y_{\hat{J}}$ and $Y_{J}$ by symmetry, so it is well-defined, and thus is $p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}$ . It is also the case for $p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}^{*}(\{\xi_{\textit{Z},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]})$ and $p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}$ .

Next, we upper bound the value of $p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}$ .

#### Claim 6.18.

The value of $p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}^{*}(\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]})$ is at most

$$ 2^{\sum_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}\left(\eta_{\textit{Y},t}-H(\xi_{\textit{Y},t})+H(\gamma_{\textit{Y},t})\right)A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\pm o(n)}. $$

Furthermore,

$$ p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}\,\leq\,2^{\sum_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}\left(\eta_{\textit{Y},t}-H(\beta_{\textit{Y},t})+H(\gamma_{\textit{Y},t})+o_{1/\varepsilon}(1)\right)A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}+o(n)}. $$

#### Proof.

We define the following two quantities:

- ( $P$ ) The number of tuples $(I,J,K,\hat{J})$ where $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ is consistent with $\{\alpha_{t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}$ , $Y_{\hat{J}}\in Y_{J}$ , and $\hat{Y}$ has complete split distributions $\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t}$ .

- ( $Q$ ) The number of tuples $(I,J,K,\hat{J})$ where $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ is consistent with $\{\alpha_{t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}$ , $Y_{\hat{J}}\in Y_{J}$ , $\hat{Y}$ has complete split distributions $\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t}$ , and additionally $Y_{\hat{J}}$ is compatible with the triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ .

Notice that by definition and by symmetry $p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}(\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]})=Q/P$ .

We first compute the simpler quantity $P$ , which is the number of level- $(\ell-1)$ block triples $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ consistent with $\{\alpha_{t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}$ (this quantity is $N_{\alpha}=2^{\sum_{t}(H(\alpha_{t})\cdot A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t})\pm o(n)}$ ) times the number of $Y_{\hat{J}}\in Y_{J}$ consistent with $\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t}$ (this quantity is $2^{\sum_{t}(H(\xi_{\textit{Y},t})-H(\gamma_{\textit{Y},t}))\cdot A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\pm o(n)}$ ). Overall,

$$ P=2^{\sum_{t}(H(\alpha_{t})+H(\xi_{\textit{Y},t})-H(\gamma_{\textit{Y},t}))\cdot A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\pm o(n)}. $$

Next, we consider how to compute $Q$ . In fact, we will show an upper bound on $Q$ (as we only need an upper bound on $p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}(\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]})$ ) by dropping the condition that “ $\hat{J}$ has complete split distributions $\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t}$ ”.

Similar to before, we have the following claim (whose proof we omit):

#### Claim 6.19.

Given a level- $(\ell-1)$ triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ that is consistent with $\{\alpha_{t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}$ , a level- $1$ block $Y_{\hat{J}}$ with $Y_{\hat{J}}\in Y_{J}$ is compatible with $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ if and only if the following hold:

- 1. For every $t\in[s^{\prime}]$ and every $(i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime})\in\mathbb{Z}^{3}_{\geq 0}\cap([0,i_{t}]\times[0,j_{t}]\times[0,k_{t}])$ with $i^{\prime}+j^{\prime}+k^{\prime}=2^{\ell-1}$ and $k^{\prime}=0$ , there is $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime}})=\beta_{\textit{Y},t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime}}$ .

- 2. For every $t\in[s^{\prime}]$ and $j^{\prime}\in\{0,\ldots,j_{t}\}$ , $\textsf{{split}}(\hat{J},S_{t,*,j^{\prime},\textup{+}})=\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Y},t,*,j^{\prime},\textup{+}}$ , where $S_{t,*,j^{\prime},\textup{+}}=\bigcup_{i^{\prime}\geq 0,k^{\prime}>0}S_{t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime}}$ .

The benefit of the above claim is that $\{S_{t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},0}\}_{t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime}}\cup\{S_{t,*,j^{\prime},\textup{+}}\}_{t,j^{\prime}}$ forms a partition of all the indices in the first region of the $t$ -th part of the interface tensor, after we fix some $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ that is consistent with $\{\alpha_{t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}$ . Thus, we can compute the possibilities of $\hat{J}$ on each of these subsets.

For $S_{t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},0}$ , the number of possibilities of $\hat{J}$ is

$$ 2^{H(\beta_{\textit{Y},t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},0})\cdot(\alpha_{t}(i^{\prime},j^{\prime},0)+\alpha_{t}(i_{t}-i^{\prime},j_{t}-j^{\prime},k_{t}-k^{\prime}))\cdot A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\pm o(n)}. $$

For $S_{t,*,j^{\prime},\textup{+}}$ , the number of possibilities of $\hat{J}$ is

$$ 2^{H(\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Y},t,*,j^{\prime},\textup{+}})\cdot(\alpha_{t}(*,j^{\prime},\textup{+})+\alpha_{t}(*,j_{t}-j^{\prime},\textup{<}))\cdot A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\pm o(n)}. $$

Thus, The total number of possible $\hat{J}$ for a fixed triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ is

$$ \displaystyle 2^{\sum_{t}\left(\sum_{i^{\prime},j^{\prime}}H(\beta_{\textit{Y},t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},0})\cdot(\alpha_{t}(i^{\prime},j^{\prime},0)+\alpha_{t}(i_{t}-i^{\prime},j_{t}-j^{\prime},k_{t}-k^{\prime}))+\sum_{j^{\prime}}H(\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}_{\textit{Y},t,*,j^{\prime},\textup{+}})\cdot(\alpha_{t}(*,j^{\prime},\textup{+})+\alpha_{t}(*,j_{t}-j^{\prime},\textup{<}))\right)\cdot A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\pm o(n)} \displaystyle={} \displaystyle 2^{\sum_{t}\eta_{\textit{Y},t}\cdot A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\pm o(n)}. $$

Multiplying the above with the number of triples $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ , we get

$$ Q\leq 2^{\sum_{t}(H(\alpha_{t})+\eta_{\textit{Y},t})\cdot A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\pm o(n)}. $$

Finally,

$$ p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}^{*}(\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]})=Q/P\leq 2^{\sum_{t}(\eta_{\textit{Y},t}-H(\xi_{\textit{Y},t})+H(\gamma_{\textit{Y},t}))\cdot A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\pm o(n)} $$

The bound (6.18) on $p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}$ follows because the $L_{\infty}$ distance between $\{\xi_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t}$ and $\{\beta_{\textit{Y},t}\}_{t}$ is at most $\varepsilon$ . ∎

The following upper bound of $p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}$ is the same as that in [VXXZ24], so we omit its proof.

#### Claim 6.20 ([VXXZ24, Claim 6.13]).

The value of $p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}^{*}(\{\xi_{\textit{Z},t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]})$ is at most

$$ 2^{\sum_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}\left(\lambda_{\textit{Z},t}-H(\xi_{\textit{Z},t})+H(\gamma_{\textit{Z},t})\right)A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\pm o(n)}. $$

Furthermore,

$$ p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}\,\leq\,2^{\sum_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}\left(\lambda_{\textit{Z},t}-H(\beta_{\textit{Z},t})+H(\gamma_{\textit{Z},t})+o_{1/\varepsilon}(1)\right)A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}+o(n)}. $$

The proof of the following claim is essentially the same as that of Claim 5.20.

#### Claim 6.21.

For every $b\in B$ , every level- $(\ell-1)$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ consistent with $\{\alpha_{t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}$ , and every typical $Z_{\hat{K}}\in Z_{K}$ , the probability that $Z_{\hat{K}}$ is compatible with multiple level- $(\ell-1)$ block triples in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{comp}}^{Z}$ is at most

$$ \frac{N_{\alpha}\cdot p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}}{N_{\textup{BZ}}\cdot M_{0}}, $$

conditioned on $h_{\textit{X}}(I)=h_{\textit{Y}}(J)=h_{\textit{Z}}(K)=b$ .

Similarly, for every $b\in B$ , every level- $(\ell-1)$ block triple $X_{I}Y_{J}Z_{K}$ consistent with $\{\alpha_{t}\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}$ , and every typical $Y_{\hat{J}}\in Y_{J}$ , the probability that $Y_{\hat{J}}$ is compatible with multiple level- $(\ell-1)$ block triples in $\mathcal{T}_{\textup{comp}}^{Y}$ is at most

$$ \frac{N_{\alpha}\cdot p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}}{N_{\textup{BY}}\cdot M_{0}}, $$

conditioned on $h_{\textit{X}}(I)=h_{\textit{Y}}(J)=h_{\textit{Z}}(K)=b$ .

Recall that we first require $M_{0}$ to be $\geq 8\cdot\frac{N_{{\alpha}_{\textit{X}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Y}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Z}}}}{N_{\textup{BX}}}$ . Now, we finalize our choice of $M_{0}$ as:

$$ \displaystyle M_{0}=\max\left\{\frac{8N_{{\alpha}_{\textit{X}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Y}},{\alpha}_{\textit{Z}}}}{N_{\textup{BX}}},\;\frac{N_{\alpha}\cdot p_{\textit{Y},\textup{comp}}}{N_{\textup{BY}}}\cdot n^{2},\;\frac{N_{\alpha}\cdot p_{\textit{Z},\textup{comp}}}{N_{\textup{BZ}}}\cdot n^{2}\right\} \displaystyle\leq 2^{\max\left\{\sum_{t}(H(\alpha_{t})-P_{\alpha,t}-H(\gamma_{\textit{X},t}))A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t},\;\;\sum_{t}(H(\alpha_{t})+\eta_{\textit{Y},t}-H(\beta_{\textit{Y},t}))A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t},\;\;\sum_{t}(H(\alpha_{t})+\lambda_{\textit{Z},t}-H(\beta_{\textit{Z},t}))A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\right\}+o(n)}. $$

We consider the fraction of holes in $Y$ -variables caused by $Y$ -compatibility zero-outs. By Claim 6.21 and by the upper bound on $M_{0}$ , the probability that each typical $Y_{\hat{J}}$ is compatible with multiple triples is at most $\frac{1}{n^{2}}$ ; the same also holds for typical level- $1$ $Z$ -blocks. As discussed earlier at the beginning of this subsection, there is another type of holes caused by the input complete split distributions, whose fraction is $O(1/n^{2})$ . Overall, we expect to get $N_{\alpha}\cdot M^{-1-o(1)}$ copies of $\mathcal{T}^{*}$ whose fraction of holes is $O(1/n^{2})$ . By Theorem 4.2, we can degenerate them into $N_{\alpha}\cdot M^{-1-o(1)}$ independent copies of unbroken $\mathcal{T}^{*}$ .

### 6.6 Summary

In conclusion, the above algorithm degenerates $\bigotimes_{t=1}^{s^{\prime}}T_{i_{t},j_{t},k_{t}}^{\otimes A_{t,1}n_{t}}\bigl[\beta_{\textit{X},t}^{(1)},\beta_{\textit{Y},t}^{(1)},\beta_{\textit{Z},t}^{(1)},\varepsilon\bigr]$ into

$$ \displaystyle N_{\alpha}\cdot M_{0}^{-1-o(1)} \displaystyle\geq{} \displaystyle 2^{\min\left\{\sum_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\cdot\left(H(\gamma_{\textit{X},t}^{(1)})-P_{\alpha,t}^{(1)}\right),\;\;\sum_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\cdot\left(H(\beta_{\textit{Y},t}^{(1)})-\eta_{\textit{Y},t}^{(1)}\right),\;\;\sum_{t\in[s^{\prime}]}A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\cdot\left(H(\beta_{\textit{Z},t}^{(1)})-\lambda_{\textit{Z},t}^{(1)}\right)\right\}-o_{1/\varepsilon}(n)-o(n)} $$

independent copies of a level- $(\ell-1)$ interface tensor $\mathcal{T}^{*}$ with parameter list

$$ \displaystyle\Big\{\Big(A_{t,1}\cdot n_{t}\cdot\bigl(\alpha^{(1)}_{t}(i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime})+\alpha^{(1)}_{t}(i_{t}\!-\!i^{\prime},j_{t}\!-\!j^{\prime},k_{t}\!-\!k^{\prime})\bigr), \displaystyle i^{\prime},\;j^{\prime},\;k^{\prime},\;\beta^{(1)}_{\textit{X},t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime}},\;\beta^{(1)}_{\textit{Y},t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime}},\;\beta^{(1)}_{\textit{Z},t,i^{\prime},j^{\prime},k^{\prime}} \displaystyle\Big)\Big\}_{t\in[s^{\prime}],\,i^{\prime}+j^{\prime}+k^{\prime}=2^{\ell-1}}. $$

The above algorithm was described for the first region; the algorithm for other regions is identical except that we permute the roles of the $X$ , $Y$ , $Z$ -dimensions. In the end, we take the tensor product over the output tensor of the algorithm over all $6$ regions.

## 7 Numerical Result

The way we combine theorems from previous sections to obtain numerical bounds on $\omega(1,\kappa,1)$ is similar to previous works (e.g., [VXXZ24]). Let $\ell^{*}>0$ be an integer denoting the highest level we hope to analyze, and let $N=2^{\ell^{*}-1}\cdot n$ . We repeatedly apply Theorems 5.3, 6.2, and 6.4 to degenerate a direct sum of $2^{o(n)}$ copies of $\mathrm{CW}_{q}^{\otimes N}\equiv\bigl(\mathrm{CW}_{q}^{\otimes 2^{\ell^{*}-1}}\bigr)^{\otimes n}$ into a direct sum of matrix multiplication tensors $\left\langle a,a^{\kappa},a\right\rangle$ , shown in Algorithm 1.

Every step of degeneration in Algorithm 1 takes a set of parameters, which includes the distribution $\alpha$ over constituent tensors, the fractions of tensor powers $A_{1},\ldots,A_{6}$ assigned to six regions, etc. Given an assignment to these parameters, we can calculate

$$ \lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\lim_{n\to\infty}V_{\ell}^{1/n},\quad\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\lim_{n\to\infty}a_{\ell}^{1/n},\quad\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\lim_{n\to\infty}b_{\ell}^{1/n},\quad\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\lim_{n\to\infty}c_{\ell}^{1/n} $$

by Theorems 5.3, 6.2, and 6.4. One can substitute them into (7) to verify a claimed bound on $\omega(1,\kappa,1)$ .

#### Optimization.

Finding the set of parameters that leads to the best bound for $\omega(1,\kappa,1)$ can be formulated as an optimization problem:

$$ \begin{array}[]{cl}\textup{minimize}&\qquad\omega^{\prime}\\
\textup{subject to}&\textup{all constraints in \lx@cref{creftypeplural~refnum}{thm:global-stage-with-eps}, \lx@cref{refnum}{thm:consituent_MM_terms}, and\lx@nobreakspace\lx@cref{refnum}{thm:constituent-stage-with-eps}}\\
&\displaystyle\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\lim_{n\to\infty}V^{1/n}\cdot\min\bigl\{A,B^{1/\kappa},C\bigr\}^{\omega^{\prime}/n}\geq(q+2)^{2^{\ell^{*}-1}}.\end{array} $$

To optimize (7), we utilize the software package SNOPT [GMS05], which employs a sequential quadratic programming (SQP) algorithm. Although SNOPT does not guarantee finding the optimal solution of the optimization problem, any feasible solution that provides a reasonably good bound on $\omega(1,\kappa,1)$ is acceptable.

[VXXZ24, Section 8] mentioned several tricks in the optimization, including setting specific initial points, using the exponential form of Lagrange multiplier constraints, and transforming minimum functions into linear inequalities. We use all of them in the same way. See [VXXZ24] for details.

#### Numerical results.

We wrote a MATLAB [Mat22] program which uses SNOPT [GMS05] to solve the optimization problem (7). By executing the program with various values of $\kappa$ , we derived upper bounds for $\omega(1,\kappa,1)$ , as listed in Table 1 (except for $\kappa=1$ , where the table states the improved bound from [DEK+26]; see below).
